data.name: Rabiyaat
data.gender_notes: Rabiyaat is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A female devotee, often used to refer to the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) beloved wife Aisha (ra). The name Rabiyaat carries the meaning “Female devotee” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Rabiyaat usually hope their child will grow to embody female devotee and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Rabiyaat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Female devotee.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rabiyaat total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: ربيات

in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم ربيات هو اسم علم مؤنث من أصل عربي، مشتق من كلمة رابعة، ويعني الرباعية أو الرابعة في الترتيب، وقد وردت هذه الكلمة في القرآن الكريم في سياق الحديث عن الأعداد والترتيبات، ويحمل هذا الاسم دلالات عددية ورمزية في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: ربیاات
in_urdu.meaning: ربیاات کا مطلب ہے چوتھا یا چوتھی منزل
in_urdu.long_meaning: ربیاات ایک علم مؤنث نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے، اس کا مطلب ہے چوتھا یا چوتھی منزل، یہ نام عربی جڑوں سے نکلا ہے اور اسلامی تقویم اور تعداد میں اہمیت رکھتا ہے، خاص طور پر جنوب ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافت میں اس کا استعمال تاریخی و ثقافتی اہمیت کا حامل ہے.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Rabiyaat" is widely used in the Islamic world to refer to female devotees of Allah, specifically those who are deeply devoted to the study and practice of Islam. It is also used as a term of endearment for Aisha bint Abu Bakr (ra), one of Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) wives, who was renowned for her piety, knowledge, and companionship with the Prophet. The term serves as a reminder of the importance of female piety and scholarship in Islam.
data.spiritual_significance: The term "Rabiyaat" holds deep spiritual significance in Islam as it represents the devoted and devotedly religious woman. By carrying the title of "Rabiyaat," a woman is identified as a servant of Allah who strives for excellence in her faith, knowledge, and moral conduct. It is a reminder of the important role that women play in the spiritual growth and development of their families, communities, and the Ummah (Muslim nation) as a whole. Additionally, the term highlights the virtues of loyalty, devotion, and love for Allah and His Messenger, qualities that every Muslim should embody.
